newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel markets hesitant, doubt crude will hold up.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel markets hesitant, doubt crude will hold up.

text.p: European fuel markets traded hesitantly on Tuesday, with much business on hold amid suspicions crude's dramatic five day rise may reverse, traders said.
With refinery margins massacred by crude's near $2 jump to two-month highs, product sellers were reluctant to lock in losses by trading precipitately.
"There has been no follow through buying on crude's rise," said one trader. "I expect we'll see some correction on the crude and then we'll see easiness returning to the product markets."
Refinery margins are in negative territory for many plant owners, which has slowed activity while operators assess their tactics.
Fuel oil barges ignored crude's strength and lost value in thin business.
After an early high sulphur barge trade at $86 a tonne fob ARA buying interest slipped lower and deals were seen at $85, $84.50 and $84, with bunker demand fairly low.
"I see the range in Rotterdam this week as $82-$87, which is not good news for refiners because with crude this strong barges should be around $89," said a trader.
"A lack of nominations and a lack of bunker demand is behind it," said another dealer. "When you see crude is up $1 yesterday and fuel is coming down, then you realise this is a pretty sick market."
At least some of the weakness stemmed from slippage in Singapore, where both paper and physical numbers have eased.
Cargo markets were quiet, though a Scandinavian refinery sold high sulphur material to a trader with a short into a British industrial user, on a floating price basis.
Some one percent material was seen on traders' books, with uncertainty over whether it would seek a home in Italy or try to work an arbitrage profit to Asia.
One percent barges were sickly, trailing well behind swaps at a nominal level of $88/$90, in line with cargo numbers. One seller was offering $89 yesterday but no business was heard done.
